chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Saqafi, from Ali ibn al-Mu'alla, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever performs wudu and wipes himself with a towel, for him is one good deed; and if he performs wudu and does not wipe himself, letting his wudu dry upon himself, for him are thirty good deeds.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in reward between wiping with a towel and letting water dry naturally after wudu?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the spiritual merit of natural drying after wudu, contrasting it with the minor reward of using a towel. This distinction reflects the Shia emphasis on mindful adherence to prophetic practices (Sunnah) in daily hygiene, where even mundane acts become opportunities for divine reward when performed with intentionality.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Saqafy, from Ali Bin Al Moalla, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Bin Humran,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who performs Ablution (Wudhu) and wipes with a towel, for him would be one Reward; but if he performs Ablution (Wudhu) and does not wipe with a towel, (letting it naturally) dry his Ablution (Wudhu) (upon himself), for him would be thirty Rewards’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafiy from Ali ibn al-Mu‘alla’ from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Humran who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
For taking Wudu’, then using a towel, one gains a good deed. Instead of using a towel if one allows the moisture from Wudu’ to dry up, one gains thirty good deeds.”
